diagnostic_interpretation: Two unchanged imported cases exceeded their 1000 ms wall-clock limit in the first full suite; the summary failure follows from 35/37 completed cases. The captured timeout stacks show DAG traversal and reachable graph compilation. Independent replays are supplementary evidence and do not erase the first failure or establish its exact GC/JIT/scheduler cause.
measurement_notes: Heavy Java validations executed sequentially; unrelated system activity was not stopped.
Each ordinary/channel/storage/cycle/soak family runs in three fresh JVMs; channel oracle and allocation backends are separate JVMs.
Java pressure settings: Java 17, G1, Xms=256 MiB, Xmx=2 GiB, Xss=1 MiB, ActiveProcessorCount=4; only runner-owned Java processes use AboveNormal priority.
Large DAG fixtures use an outer 15 s attempt deadline while internal production work/time limits remain unchanged.
Pooled nearest-rank percentiles use measured samples only. Session samples include eight queries. Cycle timing/allocation exclude supplement replanning and independent validation.
Channel includes one cold and four warmup calls per graph; storage has three warmups per shape; cycle has three per shape; ordinary planner/certificate have three and side output has one.
All short-seed cycle results, including cutoff results, are supplemented, replanned and independently replayed.
fixture_hash_normalization: SHA-256 of source bytes with CRLF normalized to LF.
limitations: Optional real EAEP artifact unavailable; corresponding JUnit test is skipped.
External awrlib unavailable; corresponding Python reader test is skipped.
Forge auto/always use fresh verification worlds with no real GTLCore installation; this is not a full modpack TPS test.
Budget/quality cutoffs do not prove global optimality; short soak does not prove absence of long-term leaks.
Original environment logs, XML, classpaths and local fixtures remain in the ignored build directory.
